hints.title: Track the exponent rather than the entire term
hints.body: The first term is 101. Taking a square root multiplies its exponent by 12, so the next two terms are 101/2 and 101/4.
hints.recap: A square root halves the exponent of a positive-base power.
hints.pitfall: Halve the exponent; do not halve the base 10.
hints.pause: Write the first four exponents and identify their common ratio.

recall.reminder: A square root halves the exponent of a positive-base power.

solution:
1. Rewrite the update as an exponent rule. If xn=10en, then xn+1=xn=10en/2. Thus en+1=12en, starting from e1=1.

2. Count the updates. There are 99 steps from term 1 to term 100, so e100=(12)99=2−99.

3. Put that exponent back on base 10. We obtain x100=10(2−99), which is C.
knowledgePattern: Track the exponent under repeated square rooting
